newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar on Thursday after the U.S. currency rose in overseas markets, dealers said.
"The shekel weakened against the dollar following the rise of the dollar abroad," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
He added that volume was low with traders net sellers of shekels by a small margin. "The business sector continues to take foreign currency-linked loans," he said.
The dealer said the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market but bought less than $100 million to support the basket.

The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to prevent the shekel from appreciating against the currency basket. The shekel has been at the bottom end of its trading band against the basket since the start of the year.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4110 shekels, against 3.4010 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7040 against 3.7029 on Tuesday.
The Bank of Israel did not set a representative rate on Wednesday because of the Jewish holiday of Shavuot.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9874 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0131 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9777 shekels compared with 1.9870 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4100 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
